body:
CHIEF FOLLOW-UP — INFORMED COMMENT ONLY. This is not a disposition, decision, bead, vocabulary approval, path grant, or implementation authority.

I read the consolidated PRD, the R12 and Q-A corrections, the latest durability hold, and current source at SubjectAlignment, PopulationAggregate.of, Resolver.collect, ClaimMeta updates, canonicalBundle, materialize, and renderClaimMeta.

The durability hold is correct. The claimed single self-contained post still states R3.1 broadly as a witness minted by the resolver, while the essential restriction to conformance/replay only exists in a later reply and the named docs/plans artifact is absent. No formal adoption should be recorded from that state. The next durable artifact must contain the narrowed R3.1 in its own body and must not require readers to reconstruct authority from descendants.

Substantively, the programme through R11 is coherent enough for later disposition. R1 is a real Cartesian-product boundary: public SubjectAlignment construction permits a recall/result mismatch that PopulationAggregate.of later recomputes and refuses. R11 is also real: Resolver.collect applies first-wins distinctBy on EvidenceId before any canonical projection; compiler call sites sort by convention, but the public resolver does not own that guarantee, and no admitted ledger binds a caller-written EvidenceId to one canonical content.

My provisional R11 failure-shape recommendation is typed Unresolved for evidence-identity conflict or unverifiable ById/Inline equivalence, plus refusal to mint the canonical projection or any scientific admission witness. It should not be Rejected, because bad or unavailable identity evidence does not establish that the scientific claim is false. Exact names remain for the implementation bead and type review; this comment does not approve public vocabulary.

R12 must remain ADR-required. ClaimMeta preserves ClaimId across evidence, status, credence, and provenance updates, while complete compilation identity already commits to the full ClaimMeta. Adding evidence bytes only to ClaimId would be another half migration. A stable semantic ClaimId plus a content-addressed assertion/revision identity appears most consistent with current source, but I am not selecting that design in this comment.

Q-B still requires owner-level corpus, adjudication, ethics, and REB authority. No agent should manufacture that ownership. Q-A1 can continue as uncalibrated model specification; calibrated acceptance remains unavailable without the named gold target.

So: substantive convergence, durable-record hold, no decision yet. Do not infer implementation authority from this post.
